snip.t: Necrotising enterocolitis: acute disorder with transmural necrosis; most common acquired GI emergency of neonates (especially premature/low birth weight); occurs most often when oral feeding initiated

qs.q: Which of the following is the most typical presenting feature of necrotising enterocolitis in premature infants?
o: It does not occur in term babies
qs.e: Abdominal distension is the hallmark sign of necrotising enterocolitis. Feeding should be stopped, and radiographs often show characteristic changes.
